title: Where to Buy Beauty & Cosmetics Online in Pakistan
summary: Where to buy beauty and cosmetics online in Pakistan: six channels compared, how to spot fake makeup with a batch code, and the COD and returns rules.
body_markdown:
Beauty and cosmetics sell online in Pakistan through six channels: brand and authorised-retailer stores, pharmacy and beauty-chain sites, large marketplaces, Instagram and WhatsApp sellers, reseller and wholesale catalogues, and cross-border apps that ship from China. They differ on one thing more than price — how confident you can be that the product inside the box is what the label says.


Pick the channel by risk. Anything that goes on your face and stays there — foundation, sunscreen, serum, lipstick — is worth buying from an authorised route. Tools, brushes, hair accessories, storage and packaging carry almost no risk, so buy those wherever they are cheapest.


Below: what each channel is good at, how to check a batch code before you pay, how to match a shade without a tester, and what returns actually cover once a seal is broken.


## The six places to buy beauty products online in Pakistan


These channels look similar in a search result and behave nothing alike once an order goes wrong. Most bad beauty orders come from buying a high-risk product in a low-accountability channel.


### 1. Brand stores and authorised retailers


International and Pakistani beauty brands sell either through their own site or through a named list of authorised retailers. This is the only channel where authenticity is not a judgement call — the chain of custody runs from the manufacturer to you.


You pay full retail. What that buys is a product with an intact seal, a readable batch code, a real expiry, and a complaint route if the batch is faulty. For active skincare and for anything applied near the eyes, that is the cheaper decision even when the number is higher.


**Best for:** sunscreen, actives (retinol, vitamin C, acids), foundation and concealer, anything for sensitive skin.


### 2. Pharmacy and beauty-chain websites


Pharmacy chains and beauty retailers with physical stores now sell online, and they inherit the store's supply chain. Stock rotates because the shelf version has to sell too, which matters for products with a short shelf life.


The practical advantage over a marketplace is that one company owns the order. There is no "the seller says" step in a complaint. The disadvantage is a narrower catalogue and fewer discounts.


**Best for:** dermatology-counter skincare, sunscreen, haircare, baby and personal-care lines.


### 3. Large marketplaces


Horizontal marketplaces carry the widest beauty catalogue in Pakistan and the most sellers per product. The same lipstick appears under a dozen store names at a dozen prices, and the listing photo is usually the brand's official image rather than a photo of that seller's stock.


That is the trap in cosmetics specifically. A copied photo tells you nothing about what is in the box. Some marketplaces run official brand storefronts inside the platform — buy from those rather than from a general seller, and read the **seller** rating and the buyer photos in the reviews, which are the only images shot on real stock. If you want the wider comparison of what the big platforms charge and how they deliver, our guide to the[best Daraz alternative in Pakistan](https://www.markaz.app/blog-post/best-daraz-alternative-in-pakistan) lays out the options side by side.


**Best for:** tools, brushes, hair accessories, packaging, and branded items bought from an official storefront.


### 4. Instagram and WhatsApp sellers


A large share of beauty selling in Pakistan happens on social. Plenty of it is honest, and the good pages are genuinely better at answering questions than any marketplace chat. It is also the channel with no listing history, no dispute system and no record of the order beyond a chat thread.


Rules that make it workable: insist on cash on delivery, ask for a video of the actual unit with the batch code visible, ask where the stock is sourced from, and check whether comments are switched off. A page that only posts a highlights reel and blocks comments has removed the one public record of how previous orders went.


**Best for:** niche and imported items a marketplace does not carry, sellers you have already bought from.


### 5. Reseller and wholesale catalogues


These exist for people buying stock rather than buying a product for themselves. Pricing sits at a reseller tier instead of a retail tier, catalogues are organised by category rather than by brand, and the platform handles delivery and cash collection. Markaz sits here — the[Markaz product categories](https://www.markaz.app/shop/categories) show how beauty, personal care and accessories are grouped, and the[supplier list](https://www.markaz.app/shop/supplier/list) shows who is actually behind the stock rather than a store name invented for a listing.


Ordinary shoppers buy here too, because the price sits below the retail markup. The trade-off is that catalogues are written for sellers: less styling, more specification. Read the listing for what the product is, not for how it is presented.


**Best for:** buying several items at once, tools and accessories, and anyone buying to resell.


### 6. Cross-border apps shipping from China


Fast-shipping apps carry the lowest stickers and an enormous catalogue of tools, brushes, lashes, nail supplies and packaging. The cost is time and uncertainty — long transit, customs handling that varies, and a return path that is rarely worth using from Pakistan.


For beauty there is one extra caution. Formulated products — anything you put on skin — travel badly and are the hardest category to verify at that distance, so keep cross-border orders to tools and hardware where the risk is a bent brush handle rather than a reaction.[Is it safe to order from China to Pakistan](https://www.markaz.app/blog-post/is-it-safe-to-order-from-china-pakistan) covers how that route works and where it goes wrong, and if you want the China catalogue with the import handled for you,[Markaz China categories](https://www.markaz.app/china/categories) land in about 10–17 days on cash on delivery with no minimum order.


**Best for:** brushes, sponges, organisers, nail and lash supplies, salon tools, packaging.


## Match the product to the channel


Risk is not spread evenly across a beauty basket. Split the order.


- **Sunscreen and active skincare.** Authorised route only. These are the products where a degraded or counterfeit formula does actual harm, and where a broken cold chain or a hot warehouse quietly ruins a genuine product.
- **Foundation, concealer and base.** Authorised route, and buy the shade only after the matching checks below.
- **Lipstick, blush, eyeshadow, mascara.** Official storefronts on a marketplace, or a brand store. Mascara is the one to be strictest about — it goes closest to the eye and has the shortest life once opened.
- **Cleansers, moisturisers and haircare.** Pharmacy sites and brand stores. Bulky, heavy, frequently repurchased, so delivery cost and stock rotation matter more here than anywhere else.
- **Brushes, sponges, tools and mirrors.** Anywhere. Marketplaces, reseller catalogues and China-direct all work; the failure mode is a disappointing tool, not a reaction.
- **Perfume and fragrance.** Its own trade with its own counterfeit problem — our roundup of the[best perfumes for women in Pakistan](https://www.markaz.app/blog-post/best-perfumes-for-women-in-pakistan) is a useful starting point for what is worth buying and what the common fakes imitate.
- **Nail, lash and salon supplies.** Reseller catalogues and China-direct. Consumables bought in quantity, low individual risk.


## How to check whether cosmetics are genuine


Counterfeit cosmetics are the reason this category needs more care than clothes or phone accessories. Fakes have improved to the point where the packaging is not a reliable tell on its own. Four checks that are.


- **The batch code.** Every genuine cosmetic carries a batch or lot code stamped or printed on the packaging — usually on the base, the crimp of a tube, or the box flap. Free batch-code lookup tools decode it into a manufacture date. Ask the seller to photograph it *before* you order. A missing, smudged, or stickered-over code is the strongest single signal that something is wrong.
- **The PAO symbol.** The small open-jar icon with "6M" or "12M" tells you how long the product stays good after opening. It should be printed with the rest of the packaging, not added on a sticker.
- **Weight and fill.** Counterfeits are usually lighter and under-filled because the shell is copied and the formula is not. If you own the genuine version, compare them in your hand.
- **Texture and smell.** A fake foundation separates faster, sits differently, and often smells faintly of solvent. Trust this one; it is the check that catches the good copies.


One thing that is not a check: price. A genuine product can be cheap because a retailer is clearing short-dated stock, and a fake can be priced near retail precisely so it does not look suspicious. Verify the unit, not the number.


## Shade matching without a tester


Buying a base shade from a photograph is the second-most common way a beauty order goes wrong. Screens shift colour, ring lights flatten undertone, and every brand numbers its shades differently.


What works: find your shade in a product you already own and note the exact brand and shade name, then look for a swatch comparison against that reference rather than against a colour chart. Ask the seller for a swatch photo taken in daylight on skin, not on paper. Buy the smaller size first if the line offers one.


Undertone matters more than depth. Two shades at the same lightness will look wrong if one is cool and you are warm, and that mismatch is visible in a photo where a half-step in depth is not. If a seller cannot tell you whether a shade runs warm, neutral or cool, they have not handled the stock.


## Expiry, heat and how beauty products travel


Cosmetics are perishable, and Pakistan's summer is hard on them. A parcel that sits in a hot van or on a warehouse shelf without air conditioning ages faster than the date on the box suggests.


Three habits worth keeping. Check the expiry or the manufacture date on arrival, before you pay the rider — not a week later. Buy sunscreen and actives in smaller sizes more often rather than stockpiling, because their shelf life is what you are actually paying for. And treat a heat-damaged product as a failed order, not as bad luck: separated foundation, a cream that has gone runny, or a lipstick that arrives soft and marked was mishandled in transit, and that is the seller's problem to fix while the parcel is still fresh.


## Cash on delivery, returns and what beauty orders actually cover


COD is the default for[online shopping in Pakistan](https://www.markaz.app/blog-post/cheapest-online-shopping-in-pakistan) and it is the main protection a first-time beauty buyer has. It stops you paying for a parcel that never arrives. It does not stop you paying for the wrong shade.


Beauty also has a returns rule that other categories do not: once a seal is broken, most sellers will not take a cosmetic back, and that is normal practice rather than a dodge — a used product cannot be resold. So the inspection that matters happens at the door, with the parcel open and the rider still there. Check the seal, the batch code, the expiry and that the shade name matches your order. Those are all visible without using anything.


Settle two things before ordering. Whether the courier allows you to open the parcel before paying, which varies by courier and by seller. And what happens if the item is damaged or wrong — in writing, before the order, not after. On Markaz, orders run on cash on delivery with a 7-day return window and local orders generally arrive in 3–5 days, so the terms belong to the platform rather than to an individual seller's mood.


## Red flags on a beauty listing


- **No batch code anywhere, and no willingness to photograph one.** The strongest single signal, and the easiest to test before you commit.
- **Only the brand's official image.** For a product where authenticity is the question, a stock photo answers nothing.
- **A luxury brand at a price that only makes sense as a mistake.** Genuine clearance exists, but it comes with a short-dated batch code the seller will happily show you.
- **"Original" repeated more than the product is described.** Listings that argue about authenticity in the title are usually the ones that need to.
- **Advance payment demanded on a first order.** On a channel where COD is normal, insisting on a transfer is a choice the seller is making for a reason.
- **No ingredient list.** If nobody will tell you what is in it, do not put it on your face.


## Buying beauty products to resell rather than to use


If you are buying stock, the question changes. You need a price you can mark up, stock you do not have to buy in bulk, and terms you can repeat to a customer without checking first.


Retail channels do not work for that. A brand store sells at the price your customer could pay directly, and a marketplace listing is visible to them too. What works is a reseller-tier catalogue: order at supplier pricing, list at your own price, and let the platform deliver and collect the cash. That is the model the[Markaz reseller programme](https://www.markaz.app/reseller-pk) runs on — no minimum order quantity, so you can list an item first and order the single unit once someone actually buys it.


Beauty has one complication that phone accessories do not: liability. You are selling something that goes on skin, so what you stock is a decision about your own customers. Start with the low-risk half of the category — brushes, sponges, organisers, mirrors, hair tools, nail supplies, packaging — where a bad unit is a refund rather than a reaction. Sell formulated skincare and makeup only where you can name the source and show a batch code, because the first customer who asks will be the one who decides your reputation.

## A routine that works


Split the basket by risk before you open a single app. Buy anything formulated from an authorised route, buy tools and hardware wherever they are cheapest, and never mix the two decisions into one order because the total looked better. Ask for a batch-code photo on anything branded. Pay on delivery, inspect at the door, and keep the packaging until the product has been on your skin once. That routine takes a few minutes and removes most of what goes wrong with buying beauty products from a photograph.


## Frequently asked questions


### Where is the cheapest place to buy beauty products online in Pakistan?


For tools, brushes and salon consumables, China-direct and reseller catalogues, which sit below the retail markup. For branded formulated products, the cheapest genuine price is usually an official storefront during a sale rather than the lowest number in the search results — below a certain price, you are no longer comparing the same product.


### How do I know if cosmetics bought online are original?


Check the batch code against a free lookup tool, confirm the PAO symbol is printed rather than stickered, compare the weight against a genuine unit if you have one, and judge the texture and smell on arrival. Ask for a batch-code photo before ordering — a seller who will not send one has answered the question.


### Is it safe to buy skincare online with cash on delivery?


COD is the safest common option because you are not paying for something that never arrives, and it gives you a moment at the door to check the seal and the expiry. It does not protect you from a wrong shade or an unsuitable formula, which is what the shade-matching and ingredient checks are for.


### Can I return makeup if the shade is wrong?


Only if the seal is unbroken. Most sellers will not accept an opened cosmetic back, which is standard practice rather than a trick. Settle the return window in writing before ordering, and do your checking at the door while the rider is still there.


### How long does delivery take for beauty products in Pakistan?


Stock already in the country usually arrives within a few days — Markaz local orders run 3–5 days. Anything shipping from China takes considerably longer; Markaz China orders land in about 10–17 days, and unmanaged cross-border parcels can take longer still.


### Can I sell beauty products online in Pakistan without buying stock in bulk?


Yes, on a no-minimum platform. Markaz has no minimum order quantity, so you can list an item and order one unit when a customer buys it. Start with tools and accessories rather than formulated skincare until you have a source you can name and a batch code you can show.
